title: TCP: Overriding of the automatic SEQ Analysis
description:
Introduce a TCP Preference allowing the overriding
of the TCP SEQ analysis with a manual interpretation.
Closes #17424.

I chose a dialog under the Analyze menu, which is intuitive for me, but indeed it's maybe a too big weapon for this. Particularly if we add similar functionalities later, then adding multiple menu entries.
One thing I was thinking was the right-clic on a packet, but shouldn't all right-clics also be accessible from a standard menu ? Moreover, I could not find the way to edit multiple TCP packets at the same time with a right-clic. The function checking the packet nature is designed for managing a single packet only.

The one exception for the right-click is the general preference section for a protocol preference. Why is this not a protocol preference for TCP? What is the reason for doing it like this, is what I would like to understand. Or to ask the question differently, would you have a trace, where some TCP packets apply this setting and some don't?

If so, it would make sense doing this in a general option

Protocol Preferences are applied globally while we are just editing the interpretation of a flagged packet. In the same conversation, one packet could be reclassified as an OoO, and another as a Retransmission.

This brought me to think it was similar to packet commenting or time-shifting (**how**: pop-up), to store in the _Analyze_ menu (**what**: change the _analysis_ behavior).

There are two limits to editing this way : it's not obvious to apply a same interpretation to multiple packets in a single action, and selecting an ordinary (not flagged) TCP packet doesn't disable the functionality.

There has to be a better solution than this dialog. It just breaks too much of what people are used with dialogs. Even a submneu would make more sense to me at this point, but the dialog just feels "off". 

Don't get me wrong, I love this functionality, and I agree, it should be part of 4.0. What bothers me is the way things are set. 

If we create a submenu in the Analyze menu with the sub-entries now present in the combobox, that would be sufficient I think. No need to implement a separate dialog for this

I stumbled upon this code and share Roland's opinions.  At this point the functionality should have some runtime to see the usefulness of it, but I really didn't like how this is the first preference in a dissector tied tightly to the GUI itself (and muddied some architectural layers). I'm going to try to come up with a better/more generic solution because it is probably too late to remove this functionality entirely.

Things have changed a lot between the first comments related to the first suggested commit and what we can see now (hopefully the comments were taken into account as much as possible).
The functionality helped some (short) time when the reassembly was not perfect when handling the retransmissions (but handling well the out-of-order), this is absolutely not the case anymore as John solved this issue and others.
Another use case is for debugging the classification itself (retransmission vs out-of-order), meaning it's more useful to developers than end users. This one also lost some meaning as we now have a better handling and less ambiguous/erroneous classification.
Probably it wasn't used by anyone but myself (I still do sometimes, when debugging as said above).
After updating manually the analysis, things aren't saved in the PCAP-NG file (it could be with a moderate effort).
In other words, not so many people would complain if this was removed. Although applying a similar idea to override a field value instead of this particular analysis could help for debugging other things, but that would need more work.
Please don't. This can be much better set by setting the data on the combo box with a Variant

The capture might have enough issues that fixing this doesn't solve it, but that is part of the problem, out of order getting marked as retransmissions.

The main issue here is, that we have 2800 protocols, and this functionality only applies to 1. That was the main reason why the protocol preferences would be the ideal place, if applies to nothing else but triggers the expectation that it does. I get, that TCP dissection is the majority of use-cases one way or another still, but again, it just breaks stuff.

Regarding 4.0, I am all for it.

Right, that makes more sense to put that in the Preferences instead. Unluckily it seems hard to move it there for these reasons :
- the protocol preferences are built dynamically from the dissectors and customizing a new behavior is not obvious (for me)
- I am currently storing in frame_data, which is different than storing a single value at the dissector level (maybe a UAT could fit, but this is in turn would probably make saving in PCAP more difficult if we had to extend that later)
- accessing the selected packet(s) from the Preferences dialog, particularly from a protocol, to read its number(s) is difficult. While I could access from the main Preferences itself (latest commit), I have no idea how to do the same from the protocol itself. If selected packets can't be read, the alternative would be to maintain manually a UAT, which is not comfortable for the end-user.

Any hint will be much appreciated.
Could it be, that the last iteration removed too much code?
Yes, I removed the previous code based on the dedicated menu, and wrote something minimal following your suggestion. A small challenge in itself to be honest :)
